summary: This lecture from Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) Part 93 explores Islamic rulings on speech and conduct, particularly focusing on prohibited behaviors. Sh. Ali Mashhour distinguishes between hadith (narrations) and sunnah (religious practices to follow), using examples from the Prophet's life. The main content covers major sins related to speech including insulting and backbiting Muslims, whispering secrets in front of others, describing women's physical features, excessive swearing by Allah's name, and unnecessary detailed descriptions of private bodily functions. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that such behaviors cause harm, remove dignity, and contradict Islamic values of respect and modesty. The lecture includes cultural critiques of modern media that openly displays bodily functions and menstruation in commercials as violations of Islamic standards of privacy and decorum.
